query: If airlines eliminated the most common cabin-service complaints in the reviews, how much would the average Overall Rating improve?

per_column.name: cabin_service_complaint_type
per_column.rationale: Directly operationalizes 'the most common cabin-service complaints' being eliminated. This is the intervention target: an airline can improve cabin service to move rows out of complaint categories (service_responsiveness, crew_attitude, food_quality, etc.) into 'no_complaint'. This is the primary treatment and it is explicitly named in the query.

per_column.name: crew_attitude_issue
per_column.rationale: A specific sub-dimension of cabin-service quality (rude/cold vs friendly). It lies on the causal path between the cabin-service lever and Overall Rating rather than being a common cause. It is an aspect of the treatment itself, implied by 'cabin-service complaints', not an independent confounder.

per_column.name: service_responsiveness
per_column.rationale: Another cabin-service dimension (attentive vs slow/refused). This is a component of the treatment/pathway, not a common cause of both treatment and outcome; adjusting for it would block part of the very effect being estimated.

per_column.name: complaint_severity
per_column.rationale: Encodes the intensity of the complaint. It characterizes the magnitude of the treatment rather than being an upstream common cause; it is post-treatment descriptive information, not a confounder.

per_column.name: complaint_resolution_quality
per_column.rationale: Whether the complaint was resolved is downstream of the complaint occurring and sits on the path to the rating. It is a post-treatment variable / mediator, so conditioning on it would bias the counterfactual effect.

per_column.name: service_failure_co_occurrence
per_column.rationale: Counts co-occurring service failures — this is a summary of the treatment's extent, on the causal pathway, not a common antecedent cause of both service quality and rating.

per_column.name: positive_service_signal
per_column.rationale: A flag for positive service mentions — the flip side of the treatment (service quality) itself. It is part of the exposure/pathway, not a confounder.

per_column.name: ground_service_complaint
per_column.rationale: Ground service is a DIFFERENT service domain that plausibly affects Overall Rating, but it is not a common cause of cabin-service complaints (it does not upstream-drive cabin service). It functions as a separate predictor/co-cause of the outcome, not a genuine confounder of the cabin-service→rating relationship.

per_column.name: cabin_class_service_gap
per_column.rationale: Service delivered relative to class expectations. This is a perception of service quality (the treatment) relative to Class; it lies on the pathway to satisfaction rather than being an exogenous common cause.

per_column.name: flight_haul_type
per_column.rationale: Haul length is a plausible common cause: longer flights create more service touchpoints (raising complaint likelihood) and also shift baseline expectations/rating levels. It is exogenous to the cabin-service lever, not on the pathway. NOT named in the query (derivable only loosely from Route), so it is the kind of confounder that demonstrates the capability under test.

per_column.name: aircraft_type_confounder
per_column.rationale: Aircraft configuration (dense narrowbody vs high-comfort widebody) is a common cause: it shapes comfort/service delivery (affecting complaints) and independently influences Overall Rating. It is a legitimate common-cause confounder and is NOT named in the query, though the heavy NULL fraction weakens its usefulness.

per_column.name: service_decline_perception
per_column.rationale: A perception that service has declined — this is downstream of the actual cabin-service quality and reflects/summarizes it on the way to the rating. It is a mediator/perceptual outcome, not a common cause.

per_column.name: service_consistency
per_column.rationale: Consistency of service across sectors is a property of the service delivered (the treatment) and sits on the pathway to the rating, not an upstream common cause of both treatment and outcome.

judge.rationale: The set clearly establishes an intervenable treatment: 'cabin_service_complaint_type' maps directly onto 'eliminating the most common cabin-service complaints', and cabin service is a lever airlines can actually set/change, so (a) is satisfied. However, the requirement (b) — supplying common causes of BOTH treatment and outcome that must be adjusted for — is only weakly met. The overwhelming majority of added columns (crew_attitude_issue, service_responsiveness, complaint_severity, complaint_resolution_quality, service_failure_co_occurrence, positive_service_signal, cabin_class_service_gap, service_decline_perception, service_consistency) are decompositions of the treatment itself or post-treatment mediators/perceptions; conditioning on them would sit ON the causal pathway and bias the counterfactual estimate rather than identify it. Only two columns, flight_haul_type and aircraft_type_confounder, are genuine exogenous common causes, and both are NOT named in the query, which is precisely the capability being tested — a positive signal. But they are diluted among many mediators, aircraft_type is ~48% NULL, and other structural confounders that would matter (Type of Traveller, Class, Airline-level quality) are not introduced as adjustment variables. Net: valid intervenable treatment, but confounder support for the interventional identification is thin and mediator-heavy.
